paper.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
paper.central_claim: Reflexion reinforces language agents not by updating weights but through linguistic feedback: agents verbally reflect on task feedback and keep their reflections in an episodic memory buffer to make better decisions in subsequent trials, improving over baselines across decision-making, reasoning and coding.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref null: subagent runtime exposes no receipt to the worker; model identity is the configured claude-kimi type only. Full text incl. Appendices A-D read.

evidence.quote: traditional reinforcement learning methods require extensive training samples and expensive model fine-tuning
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: RL for language agents needs many samples and fine-tuning.

evidence.quote: We propose Reflexion , a novel framework to reinforce language agents not by updating weights, but instead through linguistic feedback.
evidence.support_explanation: Core claim: weight-free reinforcement through linguistic feedback stored in memory.

evidence.quote: maintain their own reflective text in an episodic memory buffer
evidence.support_explanation: Persisted state = reflective text in an episodic memory buffer.

evidence.quote: it does have the disadvantages of relying on the power of the LLM’s self-evaluation capabilities (or heuristics) and not having a formal guarantee for success
evidence.support_explanation: Authors state dependence on self-evaluation and no guarantee.

evidence.quote: In practice, we bound mem by a maximum number of stored experiences
evidence.support_explanation: Memory is a bounded window (1-3 experiences); no curation or gate.

evidence.quote: we truncate the agent’s memory to the last 3 self-reflections
evidence.support_explanation: ALFWorld memory = last 3 reflections.

evidence.quote: if the agent executes the same action and receives the same response for more than 3 cycles
evidence.support_explanation: ALFWorld self-evaluation heuristic triggering reflection (hallucination / inefficient planning).

evidence.quote: In the baseline runs, if self-reflection is suggested, we skip the self-reflection process, reset the environment, and start a new trial.
evidence.support_explanation: ALFWorld baseline also gets repeated trials after reset, without memory: a fair retry control.

evidence.quote: ReAct + Reflexion significantly outperforms ReAct by completing 130 out of 134 tasks
evidence.support_explanation: ALFWorld headline: 130/134 solved over 12 trials.

evidence.quote: In the ReAct-only approach, we see that performance increase halts between trials 6 and 7.
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline plateaus while Reflexion keeps improving.

evidence.quote: we use exact match answer grading using the environment to give a binary success signal to the agent
evidence.support_explanation: HotPotQA retry signal is ground-truth exact match, i.e. an oracle on the evaluated instance.

evidence.quote: ReAct-only, CoT-only, and CoT (GT)-only implementations fail to probabilistically improve on any tasks
evidence.support_explanation: Baselines are said never to solve a previously failed question on retry at temperature 0.7 - implausible without a reported pass@k control.

evidence.quote: In the Reflexion runs, we allowed the agent to gather experience and retry on failed tasks until it produced 3 consecutive failed attempts
evidence.support_explanation: Reflexion gets up to many oracle-checked retries; baseline retry budget is not stated.

evidence.quote: self-reflection improves learning by an 8% absolute boost over the episodic memory learning advantage
evidence.support_explanation: Ablation: reflection vs raw episodic memory on CoT(GT), 100 questions.

evidence.quote: Figure 4 : Chain-of-Thought (CoT) and ReAct. Reflexion improves search, information retrieval, and reasoning capabilities on 100 HotPotQA questions.
evidence.support_explanation: HotPotQA evaluation set size = 100 questions.

evidence.quote: Then, we filter for syntactically valid test statements by attempting to construct a valid abstract syntax tree (AST) for each proposed test.
evidence.support_explanation: Self-generated tests are filtered only for syntactic validity.

evidence.quote: We set n n to a maximum of 6 unit tests.
evidence.support_explanation: At most 6 self-generated tests per problem.

evidence.quote: with a max memory limit of 1 experience
evidence.support_explanation: Programming memory limit = 1 reflection.

evidence.quote: HumanEval (PY) 0.80 0.91
evidence.support_explanation: Base 0.80 -> Reflexion 0.91 on HumanEval Python.
On MBPP Python Reflexion is below the base (0.80 -> 0.77): a reported negative result.

evidence.quote: the false positive test execution rate for MBPP Python is 16.3% while the rate for HumanEval Python is a mere 1.4%
evidence.support_explanation: Self-evaluation reliability measured: false positives explain the MBPP shortfall.

evidence.quote: Test generation omission False True 0.52
evidence.support_explanation: Omitting test generation: 0.52 vs base 0.60 (worse than baseline).

evidence.quote: Self-reflection omission True False 0.60
evidence.support_explanation: Omitting self-reflection: no gain over base 0.60 despite tests and retries - control for extra attempts.

evidence.quote: Reflexion True True 0.68
evidence.support_explanation: Full method 0.68 on the 50 hardest HumanEval Rust problems.

evidence.quote: on a subset of the 50 hardest HumanEval Rust problems
evidence.support_explanation: Ablation (and Rust result) rests on n=50 problems.

evidence.quote: Baseline 0.26 0.00481 Reflexion 0.26 0.00305
evidence.support_explanation: StarChat-beta: no gain (0.26 vs 0.26, std over 8 trials).

evidence.quote: We found that the ability to specify self-corrections is an emergent quality of stronger, larger models.
evidence.support_explanation: Boundary: needs strong models.

evidence.quote: after only four trials, we terminate the runs as the agent does not show signs of improvement
evidence.support_explanation: WebShop: no improvement; runs stopped after four trials.

evidence.quote: Reflexion is unable to solve tasks that require a significant amount of diversity and exploration
evidence.support_explanation: Stated failure regime.

evidence.quote: it may still succumb to non-optimal local minima solutions
evidence.support_explanation: Stated limitation.

evidence.quote: LeetcodeHardGym, which is an interactive programming gym that contains 40 Leetcode hard-rated questions that have been released after October 8, 2022, which is the pre-training cutoff date of GPT-4
evidence.support_explanation: New post-cutoff benchmark of 40 problems (contamination control for one dataset only).

evidence.quote: Reflexion achieves a 91% pass@1 accuracy on the HumanEval coding benchmark, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art GPT-4 that achieves 80%
evidence.support_explanation: Headline code claim.

evidence.quote: The base strategy is a single code generation sample.
evidence.support_explanation: Baseline = one sample; Reflexion uses iterative generation + tests: compute is not matched.

evidence.quote: the generated code is not validated before execution
evidence.support_explanation: Authors warn that code is executed unvalidated (sandboxing advice).

evidence.quote: self-reflection model generates nuanced and specific feedback
evidence.support_explanation: Reflection model generates the text that is stored (mechanism).

evidence.quote: Self-Refine [ 15 ] employs an iterative framework for self-refinement to autonomously improve generation through self-evaluation
evidence.support_explanation: Closest neighbor named: Self-Refine (single-generation, no memory).

Searched: each task instance keeps its own memory, reset between instances; no experiment carries reflections to different questions/environments or evaluates on instances that did not produce the reflections. Gains are across trials of the same instance.
No confidence intervals, seeds or significance tests for the main results; only Table 4 reports a std (StarChat). Sets: 134 ALFWorld envs, 100 HotPotQA, 40 LeetcodeHardGym, 50 Rust problems.
No token/call counts, number of trials for code, or wall-clock are reported; compute of Reflexion (multi-trial + tests + reflection) vs single-sample baselines is not stated.

signatures.object: Per-task episodic memory buffer of self-written reflections injected into the actor prompt (policy theta = {LLM, mem}).
signatures.information: Actor sees previous reflections (window 1-3) and its current trajectory; reflector sees trajectory + scalar/binary feedback; evaluator may be exact-match oracle (HotPotQA), env success + heuristic or LLM self-eval (ALFWorld), or self-generated unit tests (code).
signatures.operation: Run trial -> evaluate -> LLM writes verbal reflection -> append to memory -> retry until pass or max trials.
signatures.output: Final trial output; memory contents are task-instance specific.
signatures.conditions: Strong instruction-following LLM (GPT-3/GPT-3.5/GPT-4 class); reliable-enough evaluator.
signatures.feedback: Sparse binary reward amplified to text; for code, self-generated tests (<=6, AST-filtered) executed in interpreter/compiler.
signatures.selection_rule: None for memory content (append; keep last Omega); for code, stop early when self-tests pass.
signatures.persistence: Within-task only; sliding window; reset per instance.
signatures.later_use: Next trial of the same instance reads memory.
signatures.claimed_effect: ALFWorld +22 points, HotPotQA +20, HumanEval +11 over baselines; reflection beats raw episodic memory.
signatures.failure_boundary: MBPP-Py false positives; StarChat and WebShop show no gain; local minima; needs strong LLM.

gap.author_gap: Language agents cannot learn quickly from trial and error: RL needs many samples and fine-tuning; prior self-refinement methods are single-generation and lack persistent memory.
gap.checked_gap: The gap (sparse scalar reward -> hard credit assignment; no cross-trial memory in Self-Refine/Beam search/CodeT/Self-Debugging) is concrete and compared in two feature tables. The "no weight updates" framing is background, not the gap. Memory-based agents of the same period are not contrasted in detail.
lineage: Self-Refine, Pryzant et al. prompt optimisation, Paul et al. critic, Xie et al. beam search, Yoran/Nair deciders, Kim retry (related work)
gap.closest_adjacent: Self-Refine (iterative self-feedback without persistent memory) and Self-Debugging (executes code feedback but no reflection/memory) as stated in the paper.
gap.residue: Whether text memory yields lasting, transferable improvement beyond retrying the same instance is not addressed.
gap.stakes: Quick, cheap, interpretable learning for deployed black-box agents.
gap.method_response: Convert scalar feedback to verbal reflection and carry it as memory into the next trial.
gap.remaining_gap: Cross-task transfer, memory curation, reliability of self-evaluation, exploration-heavy tasks.
unresolved: Contemporary memory/reflection agents (e.g. generative agents cited only in the intro) are not compared; no pinned copies.

rs_pattern.reason: Primary: sparse environment reward / absent hidden tests are replaced by a model-generated signal (verbal reflection and self-written unit tests, with a syntactic filter) used to adapt the next attempt. Sub-cards do not fit (C07 internal-state stability, C08 data factory, C26 preference objective). Supporting (partial): adaptation happens purely by in-context conditioning on stored text instead of weight updates (adapt_via_conditioning); C03 (multi-task schema tuning) is not executed. Considered and rejected: reframe/assumption_audit.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: diagnosis of what the proxy corrects: partial (credit assignment, FP/FN analysis of tests); curation/filter whose removal breaks the method: partial (AST filter; ablation shows omitting test generation hurts); noisy self-estimates made relative: no; causal intervention: partial (omit reflection / replace with raw episodic memory); realistic setting: partial (HotPotQA retry uses oracle EM).
matches.success_failure_checks: Failure "assumption (calibration) that fails" - applies to self-tests (16% FP on MBPP-Py); "no isolating baseline" - applies to HotPotQA/ALFWorld heuristic.
matches.reason: The load-bearing step is generating the supervisory text/tests from the model itself.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: conditioning channel is prompt-only (not trained as a modality); no structural holdout; mechanism-isolating ablation present (reflection vs episodic memory vs none); contamination analysis only for LeetcodeHardGym.
matches.success_failure_checks: Failure "works only under idealized assumptions / decays with weaker model" - observed (StarChat, WebShop).
matches.reason: The retained state is injected as conditioning; this is a distinct operation from generating the signal.

rs_pattern.executes_pattern: partial (signal generation executed; conditioning without trained channel).
rs_pattern.resolves_problem: partial: within-instance retry success improves on tasks with a reliable evaluator; learning that persists across tasks is not shown.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS "derive an adaptation signal from the model's own outputs" <-> domain "reflect on outcomes into lessons stored and injected into later contexts": the reflection IS the manufactured signal.
pattern_mapping.required_conditions_or_differences: Domain H00 expects transfer beyond retries and separation of lesson and evaluation streams; Reflexion is within-instance with shared stream.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS conditioning-not-retraining <-> domain store injected into later context with the model frozen.
pattern_mapping.required_conditions_or_differences: Frozen model only; domain card additionally wants a store maintenance/edit policy (H01) which is absent.

expectations.reason: Reflections serve later trials of the same item; no test on other items.
Feedback source and scored instance coincide; on HotPotQA the retry signal is the ground-truth answer.

expectations.applies_when: Gain attributed to the stored lessons.
expectations.reason: Store-off arms exist (ALFWorld memoryless retries, code self-reflection omission, EPM) but compute/retry budgets are not matched for HotPotQA and not stated for code.
No gate or versioning; all reflections appended and old ones dropped by window.

expectations.applies_when: Self-judge decides what becomes a lesson.
expectations.reason: Grounding signals are explicit (env, heuristic, self-tests) and the self-judge imperfection is quantified for code.
Isolating baselines exist for ALFWorld and code but not for HotPotQA, where oracle-checked retries are also available to the method only.
Post-cutoff LeetcodeHardGym (n=40) is the only contamination control; HumanEval/MBPP/HotPotQA not analysed.

claims.text: ReAct+Reflexion solves 130/134 ALFWorld tasks within 12 trials, +22 points over strong baselines.
claims.setting: 134 fixed environments; trial loop with environment reset; GPT-3 actor (as in ReAct).
claims.baseline_control: ReAct with resets but no reflection.
claims.selection_vs_test: Same environments provide the feedback and are scored; heuristic/LLM self-eval triggers reflection.
claims.result_denominator: 134 tasks, cumulative success curve; single run.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Memory of reflections improves cumulative within-environment success beyond memoryless retries; no evidence of learning that carries to new environments.

claims.text: Reflexion improves HotPotQA reasoning/search by up to 20%, and reflection beats episodic memory by 8%.
claims.baseline_control: Baselines claimed unable to improve on retry (T=0.7); EPM ablation.
claims.selection_vs_test: Binary ground-truth EM tells the agent when to retry.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Given an oracle correctness signal, reflection-conditioned retries solve more questions than the described baselines; the oracle and unmatched retries limit the claim.

claims.text: Reflexion reaches 91% pass@1 on HumanEval (Python), surpassing GPT-4 80%; also improves Rust and LeetcodeHardGym.
claims.setting: Self-generated tests (<=6) drive reflection; final answer judged on hidden benchmark tests.
claims.selection_vs_test: Loop uses self-tests only; scoring uses benchmark tests (decoupled).
claims.allowed_conclusion: Iterative self-test + reflection beats a single sample on several code sets (not MBPP-Py, not a weak model); compute not matched and reflection-free retries were tested only on Rust-50.

claims.text: Failures are bounded: Reflexion does not help weak models or exploration-heavy tasks.
claims.result_denominator: StarChat 0.26 vs 0.26; WebShop 100 envs stopped after 4 trials.

assessment.evidence_level_note: Improvement is across trials on the same instances that provide the feedback (oracle on HotPotQA); memory is per instance and reset, so no retained-for-later-tasks evidence. Ablations support the role of reflection text within the retry loop.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On tasks with a usable per-instance feedback signal and a strong LLM, storing self-written reflections raises success over repeated trials relative to memoryless retries and to raw trajectory memory, with honest negative cases (MBPP-Py, weak models, WebShop).
unresolved: transfer of reflections to unseen instances

G.reason: Credit-assignment gap and missing persistent memory in neighbors are specific and tabulated against Self-Refine, beam search, CodeT, Self-Debugging; "no weight update" is background only. Neighbor comparison is coarse and later memory agents are not covered.

M.reason: Three-role mechanism explains how a scalar becomes actionable text, with a testable prediction (reflection > raw memory > none) and acknowledged dependence on evaluator quality.

X.reason: Loop, evaluators, memory window sizes, test generation and filter are reproducible; failure regimes and false-positive behavior are reported. No retention gate, curation, versioning or cross-task store exists, so X for retention-type conditions is thin.

E.measurement.reason: Standard benchmarks and decoupled hidden tests for code, but HotPotQA success is judged by the same ground truth that drives retries, small sets (100/50/40), and the 91% number compares multi-trial vs single sample.

E.causality.reason: Matching ablations in each domain (memoryless retry in ALFWorld, EPM vs reflection, test-generation and reflection omission) isolate the reflection text; missing: pass@k control for HotPotQA baselines, compute matching, cross-instance memory.

E.holdout.reason: Feedback and evaluation share instances (oracle for HotPotQA); no held-out instances for learned memory; contamination control only for LeetcodeHardGym.

E.statistics.reason: Single runs, no intervals or seeds except one std for StarChat; small n (100/50/40); 0.60->0.68 on Rust-50 is four problems.

E.cost.reason: No call/token/trial counts; baselines are single-sample for code and have unstated retry budgets for HotPotQA.

rationale: Clear, reproducible reflect-and-retry loop with real ablations and honest negative cases, but memory is per-instance (no cross-task retention), HotPotQA uses an oracle signal, single runs and no cost accounting.
